Quarterly revenue grew by twelve percent year over year, beating internal forecast and street consensus by a comfortable margin.
Customer churn dropped to its lowest level in two years across all market segments and product lines, with enterprise retention reaching a record high.
Three new enterprise accounts signed during the period with multi-year commitments, expanding the named-account roster into two new verticals.
Gross margin expanded by two hundred basis points on improved infrastructure costs, lower third-party data licensing fees, and disciplined hosting renegotiations.
Product engineering shipped four major feature releases across the platform this quarter, including the long-awaited collaboration suite and the new mobile experience.
Operating expenses came in below plan despite continued investment in headcount and go-to-market, with disciplined spend management throughout the organization.
Sales pipeline coverage exiting the quarter sits comfortably above three times the next-quarter target with a healthier mid-funnel mix than a year ago.
Net dollar retention crossed one hundred and twenty percent for the first time, reflecting both expansion within existing accounts and reduced contraction.
